target_customer: Colocation, modular and AI data center operators and infrastructure lenders
problem: Data center operators juggle separate BMS, EPMS, SCADA, NOC and DCIM tools that take months to roll out. Aravolta combines them in one platform deployable in days.
business_model: B2B software with per-device pricing, no per-point fees (quotes on request)
product_category: Data center infrastructure management and monitoring software

founders.name: Margarita Groisman
founders.background_notes: Per YC bio. Education not listed.

founders.name: Jack Sutton
founders.background_notes: YC bio says lifelong software engineer; no employers or education listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting many industrial and IT protocols (SNMP, Modbus, BACnet, OPC-UA, Redfish) into one monitoring and control product is integration heavy but standard engineering; control of live power systems raises reliability stakes.

defensibility.rationale: Once wired into operations and power systems the platform is sticky, but entrenched DCIM vendors such as Schneider and Nlyte sell similar suites.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features during 2025 and Nlyte planned an agentic framework for Q1 2026, per a trade article.

market_need_then: The AI build out drove rapid data center construction, and operators faced months long DCIM rollouts, with capital raises for data center tech startups reported in 2025.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and confident with short punchy lines such as Your call and Days, not months

branding.community_and_virality: A podcast episode featured the CEO; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive volt suggestive name and crisp voice, but little brand press or community and no source ties the brand to growth.

outcome_analysis: Aravolta is active and raised a reported 5.1 million dollar seed in December 2025 after the Spring 2025 batch, riding the data center build out. The CEO's Microsoft data center experience fits the problem, and it lists many colocation customers. Entrenched DCIM vendors with AI features keep risk high, so the outcome is open.
notes: Seed of 5.1M is reported by StartupIntros, Signalbase and FundedIQ, and a Business Wire release of 2025-12-19 announces new capital; that release returned 403 and was not opened, so lead investors are unknown beyond one angel. A separate 100K seed from Orange DAO appears in a June 2025 capital raises list (Castle Placement, snippet only) and is not recorded. Competition empty: sources found were not dated near the batch. No outcome news found.
